processing: A tea plant cultivar rather than a finished style; it is mostly pan-fired and pressed flat into Longjing, in the usual method for that tea.
harvest_season: Spring. As with other Longjing, the picking before Qingming is the most prized; exact budding dates for this cultivar are not well published.
appearance_dry: Pointed, slim, flat and smooth leaves, green with a slight yellow cast.
appearance_liquor: Clear pale yellow-green, as is typical of a good Longjing.
appearance_wet: Long, slender tender leaf and bud, as the cultivar's name suggests, bright yellow-green.
taste_profile: High, clean fragrance with a fresh, mellow savour; the rest follows the familiar pattern of Longjing, with a soft nutty sweetness.

brewing.notes: Brew as any Longjing: water around 80 C, a glass or wide cup, and no lid trapping the steam.

vintage_note: Sold as Longjing of the current spring, usually under the name of its production zone rather than the cultivar. Earlier picks cost more. Drink within a year and keep it sealed and cool.
description:
Longjing Changye, 'Longjing long leaf', is a tea plant bred from the Longjing population, not a separate kind of tea. You will mostly drink it without knowing: it goes into Longjing, and it is one of the main cultivars of the Yuezhou production zone, with some planting in the Xihu area too.

Made the Longjing way, in a hot wok by pressing the leaf flat, it gives a slim, pointed, smooth leaf with a touch of yellow in the green. It has a reputation for working well in higher grades, because the leaf shapes neatly.

In the cup, expect a clear, lifted aroma and a fresh, mellow taste. Detailed comparisons with Longjing 43 or the old population plants are hard to find, so the best way to know it is side by side. Use water around 80 C and do not overdo the leaf.

Few shops list the cultivar, so ask.
history: Breeding is credited to the Tea Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, which selected it from the Longjing plant population by single-plant selection between 1960 and 1987. It is held in the national tea germplasm collection, noted for its slender leaves.
